summary: Test-only control for CONF3's recovery-flat branch, re-reviewed on the fresh head 72bc9db (the b22f73b1 path was poisoned by MY pin-commit error, not by anything in the change). Head verified: base 0b9d16b7 is current origin/main, diff vs base is one line — tests/unit/test_confirmation_exit_fanout.py 38/0 — and git diff over src/ is EMPTY, so production code is byte-identical to base. The new commit 72bc9db is genuinely EMPTY (git show --stat lists no files) and the tree is byte-identical to b22f73b1, which I confirmed by diffing the two heads directly rather than taking it on trust. THE DECISIVE CHECK, re-run on this head rather than carried forward: removing _end_confirmation_unprotected_interval(resolution=flat) from _recover_released_confirmation_webull_leg at service.py:3981 — the exact source location that left ALL 17 fan-out tests GREEN when I mutated it during the #902 review — now turns test_recovery_flat_finalizes_released_unprotected_interval RED at released_unprotected_seconds_max=0.000 instead of 4.000. Restored: 18/18. The previously inert branch is now pinned by a control that can come out false. The test advances a monkeypatched clock by exactly 4s inside the broker read, so 4.000 is deterministic and not wall-clock flake, and it also asserts the durable Webull managed row is closed, that (WEBULL, SYMBOL) has left _confirmation_unprotected_since, that COVERAGE-RESTORED is emitted with resolution=managed_episode_closed, and that both the per-leg seconds and the summary max carry 4.000. I ACCEPT AND HAVE INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED CODEX-2'S CORRECTION OF MY OWN #902 PIN, two ways rather than taking it: (1) code — _close_confirmation_flat_leg calls _clear_exit_reservation_release on a successful close, and that function pops the key from _confirmation_unprotected_since and emits COVERAGE-RESTORED, so the live current count is already cleared on this path independently of the finalizer; (2) the mutant's own output — released_unprotected_current=0 appears in BOTH the passing and the failing run, so it was never inflated. My #902 pin described the regression as leaving the symbol in _confirmation_unprotected_since and inflating released_unprotected_current; THAT MECHANISM WAS FALSE. The real regression is narrower — the elapsed interval is lost from the decision summary. The conclusion that the branch needed a control still stands and this PR supplies it. Recorded append-only at corrections/pr-902-uncovered-current-count.md, already on origin/review-pins, per the #898 precedent. My root error there: I asserted a runtime consequence from reading one call site without asking who else writes that state; the counter had a second writer. NOT COVERED: this pins the MEASUREMENT of the uncovered interval, not the live close — post-#897 the confirmation exit has still never fired in production and no test can supply that. PR MERGEABLE; validate was rerunning on this head at review time and must be green before merge.
